hook.text: Every company has more jobs to be done than resources available to do those jobs.

summary.tone: Calm, confident corporate explainer: friendly mascot-and-aurora brand bookends around plain, factual real-product demos, with a measured reassuring VO that ends on trust and safety.

signature_moments.description: The opening agent mind-map: six agent cards pop in and sprout task chips with connector lines while the mascot flies through, visualising 'more jobs than resources'.
signature_moments.why_premium: It turns an abstract pain line into a dense, staggered motion-graphic system in five seconds, so the problem feels concrete and branded before any product UI appears.

signature_moments.description: The guardrail test: an unsafe prompt is routed by the plan trace to Inappropriate_Content and the agent refuses, shown side by side with the chat.
signature_moments.why_premium: Showing the reasoning trace next to the conversation proves the trust claim with real product behaviour instead of asserting it, which is rare and persuasive.

signature_moments.description: The final screen recording shrinks into a floating rounded card over the aurora, then pushes away to reveal the mascot and logo end card.
signature_moments.why_premium: Reframing the raw UI as an object inside the brand world stitches the demo back into the motion-graphic bookends and gives the ending a deliberate, polished resolve.

hook.evidence: A relatable pain line (w0-w14) over a lively mind-map is competent, but it is a generic business truism with no surprise, stat or product glimpse in the first seconds.

clarity.evidence: Simple structure: what it is (s002-s003), three concrete agent examples each with a matching UI (s004-s008), how to build one (s009 w103-w160) and why it is safe (w161-w201); each VO clause lines up with a visible UI step. The 41 s single take in s009 has no zooms or callouts, so small UI detail is hard to follow.

ui_showcase.evidence: Real product UI throughout: service chat, CRM leads list, Gmail booking, live sales-coach call and the Agent Builder flow ending in a guarded refusal. Authentic and varied, but shown as flat full-frame recordings without camera push-ins, highlights or cropping to the relevant panel.

motion_polish.evidence: The bookends (s001-s003, s010-s011) are polished: staggered card pops, motion-blurred mascot, vertical pushes and a card-shrink outro. The middle is largely untreated screen recording joined by horizontal pushes, with s009 a 41 s static-framed take.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchors plus visuals: a continuous music bed at 129.2 BPM with integrated loudness -24.57 LUFS (quiet for web), and 54 detected audio events labelled mostly music/chime/unsure (e.g. x019 chime at 33.07 s, x029 chime at 57.06 s), suggesting soft accents rather than tightly synced UI SFX; pushes do not show clear whoosh hits. Competent but understated; I cannot hear the mix itself.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Tight, parallel structure ('Like an AI service agent... or an AI sales development agent... or an AI sales coach agent') and a strong trust close ('refusing to be lured outside those guardrails', w183-w201; 'the confidence to deploy autonomous AI agents', w202-w220). Some long run-on sentences and the generic opener keep it below best-in-class.

brand_consistency.evidence: Mascot, aurora/mountain illustration and geometric sans recur at open and close (s001-s002, s011), and the product UI is all Salesforce; the middle demos drop the brand world entirely until the s010 card reframing pulls it back.

works_muted.evidence: No captions or explanatory overlays; the title card and UI demos (chat answering, meeting booking, refusal) are partly self-explanatory, but the agent types, the custom-agent process and the guardrail message live almost entirely in the VO.

overall.evidence: A clear, trustworthy product explainer with branded motion-graphic bookends and authentic demos, including a strong guardrail proof; the long untreated screen recordings, quiet understated audio and lack of captions keep it at competent rather than premium.

localization_friendliness.notes: Designed text is minimal (agent card labels in s001, the 'Agentforce / What is Agentforce?' title, the end-card URL) and easy to re-render, but all product screens are English UI recordings that would need re-capture, and the narrative depends on the VO, so a new language needs a new voice track plus re-shot demos.
